done: Guessed the resolved-invocation type was called Resolved from the README's variable naming; it is actually Resolution. Model::problems() was dead code from the plain binary's perspective even with a passing test calling it, since #[cfg(test)] code is not compiled into that target at all - fixed by having main() call it as a genuine startup self-check on each command's own contract, which is itself consistent with [drift-detection](concepts.md#drift-detection) (verify, do not just trust). A stable-resolved indexmap version needed edition2024, which the declared MSRV (1.75.0) cannot parse; pinned it explicitly and, in fixing this, found Cargo.lock was gitignored (inherited from the rustnix template's generic default) - fixed to be tracked, since a binary crate needs its lockfile committed for an MSRV pin to survive a fresh clone or CI run at all.

considered: JSON/JSONC for the manifest, matching Wrangler's own current recommendation.
done: Researched the JSON/YAML/TOML tradeoffs specifically for a hand-editable, cross-language project manifest rather than a deeply nested orchestration config (see [manifest-file-format](concepts.md#manifest-file-format)): TOML's comment support and lack of YAML's implicit-typing and indentation footguns fit a manifest people edit by hand, and its array-of-tables syntax matches "a list of modules" directly. Found and weighed the honest counter-case before committing: Cloudflare's Wrangler moved away from TOML-only specifically over its array-of-tables footgun in a heavily hand-edited config - judged as a smaller risk here because the manifest is meant to be edited through add/import/remove rather than freehand, and per-module detail lives in each fork's own .rhizoid/module.toml rather than in one large top-level file (see [distributed-state-no-lockfile](concepts.md#distributed-state-no-lockfile)). Also decided, separately and far more simply: auth goes through an already-authenticated gh for now (see [auth-via-gh](concepts.md#auth-via-gh)), rather than Rhizoid managing its own credentials.
rejected: JSONC is not a real standard (every parser's comment-stripping behavior differs slightly) and lacks TOML's native date/array-of-tables types; the footgun that pushed Wrangler away from TOML applies less here given how the manifest is actually meant to be edited.
title: Decided the manifest format (TOML) and that auth goes through gh for now

done: This plan covers the fork-management side only: how Rhizoid forks, tracks, and syncs dependencies into a configured org. How a third repo (something that is not Rhizoid itself) declares "I depend on this org's fork of X at version Y" and pulls it in remains a separate, undesigned problem, kept apart on purpose since the first reflection on this project.
title: Kept the consumption-side manifest deferred, distinct from this plan

done: Dependabot opened a real PR within minutes of rustnix going live, proposing dtolnay/rust-toolchain@1.75.0 -> @1.120.0 in the msrv job - it cannot tell a version pinned as a floor to test against from a version to keep current. Closed the PR without merging and added a Dependabot ignore rule.
title: Found and fixed Dependabot silently defeating the MSRV job

considered: Assuming argenv worked like a typical CLI-parsing crate (subcommands, positional arguments) from its description alone.
done: Fetched argenv's actual API (Input/Arg/Env, the resolve/lint functions) and argenv-cli's own main.rs rather than assuming a clap-like shape from its one-line description. Found it declares flags and environment variables only - no subcommands, no positional arguments (see [argenv-is-flags-and-env-only](concepts.md#argenv-is-flags-and-env-only)). Settled the boundary layer's shape on that basis: a two-crate workspace, rhizoid-core and rhizoid-cli (see [rhizoid-crate-shape](concepts.md#rhizoid-crate-shape)), a hand-written verb dispatcher matching argenv-cli's own reference pattern, argenv Models for each command's named flags (with env fallback, so CI/scripts can drive Rhizoid without touching argv at all), and manifest infrastructure (Manifest/Module types, TOML read/write, a schemars-derived schema, a schema subcommand mirroring argenv-cli's own). The real git/gh operations behind GitPort/GitHubPort are explicitly out of scope for this pass - each command resolves and validates its inputs and loads the manifest, and either does the one thing that needs no GitHub (init) or reports plainly that the rest is not implemented yet.
rejected: Would have produced a design that does not compile against the real crate. Reading the actual source first cost a handful of API calls and avoided building the wrong thing.
title: Read argenv's real source before designing the boundary layer around it

considered: A single add command with a flag choosing create-vs-adopt behavior, and folding status and a Terraform-style separate plan into one command.
done: Seven verbs for v1 (see [rhizoid-command-surface](concepts.md#rhizoid-command-surface)): init, add, import, update, status, refresh, remove. send-upstream (clean patch back to the true upstream) is real and designed but deferred to v0.2, after the core loop is proven on real dependencies. Each managed fork carries its own .rhizoid/module.toml (see [module-metadata-file](concepts.md#module-metadata-file)), mirroring .tad/.gitrepo's pattern already proven in the tad system: a plain, readable file is the source of truth for a module's state, not something buried in commit messages or a separate database.
rejected: A flag with a default is exactly the kind of thing that goes wrong quietly - kept add and import as separate verbs instead, matching Terraform's own precedent (see [adopt-vs-create](concepts.md#adopt-vs-create)). Folding plan into status was kept, though: unlike cloud infrastructure, inspecting local git state and GitHub's API is cheap and side-effect-free, so there is no real cost to always doing it - no need for a separate read-only-vs-mutating split the way Terraform needs one.
title: Settled the v1 command surface and the fork's own metadata file

done: Two-crate workspace in git-rhizoid/rhizoid (rhizoid-core, rhizoid-cli - see [rhizoid-crate-shape](concepts.md#rhizoid-crate-shape)). init and remove are fully working, needing no GitHub; the other five (add, import, update, status, refresh) resolve and validate their inputs against a real argenv Model, then report plainly that they are not implemented yet rather than pretending to work. Verified locally and on real GitHub Actions, including the MSRV job.

rejected: That: it painted an idea as a failure.
title: Not yet is not failure

considered: Requiring a project prefix on every criterion.
done: A milestone's criteria are read in its own project first, then anywhere - needed once a path (Rhizoid's) read another project's backlog on purpose; lenses the observatory finds but does not curate are shown under their own heading.
rejected: That: own-first reads naturally, and chaining stays one word.
title: Criteria in their own project; discovered lenses

considered: A bolder dot.
done: Looking at screenshots of the Russian pages: unknown cells read as blank (the faint dot is now a clear ?); the table's first column was named from a table name (the lens names its rows); categories came in an arbitrary order (the lens orders its groups, by the source category so it holds in every language); the milestone cards' chips were English (now messages). A second look showed the question marks white on pale: the table's "cell text is white" rule outranked the pale cells' own - the real cause of the invisible sign; their rule now outranks it, with a test.
rejected: That: a question mark says unknown without a legend.
title: Four things only eyes found

considered: Depending on ocoeco's code; restructuring every formatting call for messages; translating rendered pages.
done: The site, the path, a page per project, made by work, grand views drawn from lenses, one site per language with Fluent catalogs, each project's own data translations; the mark, discovery and harvest moved out to ocoeco; renamed ocoeco-engine.
rejected: Hard-coded grand views; unknown counted as failure; readiness from any done milestone; a lens translating other projects' data.
title: From a first site to ocoeco's rendering engine

considered: Reordering and rewording the cards.
done: Said by the author: the Idea tab told a commoner nothing - terse cards, alphabetical, written about a project rather than by it. A project's idea is now an ordered piece of writing in its own data, shown as an article; a lens opens with the idea of what it is about.
rejected: That: cards name the parts for an insider; an idea is read from the start by someone who knows nothing.
title: The idea, as an article

considered: A longer cut; a smaller font.
done: The path's labels ran into each other (reported with a screenshot): the path is now page layout - a cell per stop, labels shown whole and wrapping inside their own cell, scrolling sideways when narrow - with a test that forbids words inside SVG.
rejected: Both: they hide the fault until the next longer title or language.
title: Words never overlap

considered: Fixing only the doubled count.
done: Found by looking at the front page: a doubled count on the grand cards, and behind it sentences in English written into the code. Both fixed; a test holds the card to one count and to words from the catalog.
rejected: That: the cause was words outside the catalog.
title: The cards speak the reader's language

done: Seen by looking at the Russian phone page: a count read '1 of 6', and each working's kind - tool, check, test - stayed English. The count is a plain fraction now and the kinds are words from the catalog.
rejected: Leaving small labels untranslated as 'technical'.
title: The last English words on a Russian page

considered: A separate page for the measure.
done: The four marks were computed inside one page; they are now one function, used by the Essence page, by every project's card on the front page, and by a single count of how many projects tell their whole essence - the same rule ocoeco check applies at home.
rejected: That: it belongs where the projects are listed.
title: The whole picture of essence, at a glance

considered: -oco on every name.
done: From two messages of the author: how a project works belongs to the project, and its idea must tell anyone what it is. Specified in ocoeco (idea, path, workings, work); the engine shows the idea as an article; four ideas written in their own repositories; the Rhizome lens opens with Rhizome's own idea.
rejected: Nothing renamed: recommended for organizations only, and left to the author.
title: A project, whole; ideas told for anyone

considered: Forcing the merge on argenv's protected branch.
done: In the phone's lab a silent speaker is now a regression like any other (health --hear; 24 checks in the baseline), with the rule made honest: a run that did not listen is not asked what only listening tells. On the Essence page a step with no workings says whether it is a wish or an untold delivery. Rhizoid wrote its workings; argenv's essence waits on its protected branch for its author.
rejected: That: the protection is the author's decision.
title: The ear in health; two kinds of gap

considered: Essence as a section of a specification.
done: Essence became its own project - the method, describing itself, with the first workings anyone has written - and the signature view: every project lands on one page that shows why, what, how and now. In the phone's lab, devlab hear played a tone on each speaker and heard both through a microphone: the first evidence there that a machine heard.
rejected: That alone - and an essay with no check.
title: Essence, a method and a view; the lab can hear

considered: Filling every step so the marks turn green.
done: Linux Phones and the phone in its lab, ocoeco, the engine, the observatory, devlab and lab-agent each wrote their workings - and their idea where none existed - in their own repositories; the Linux Phones lens opens with its essence and gives the phone its own page. The measure reads true: most projects stand at three marks of four, none at four.
rejected: That: the gaps are the list of what to build.
title: The essence of eight more projects

considered: tad as a top tab; renaming tad-engine in place; the engine depending on ocoeco's code.
done: The path for every subject (three horizons, milestones filled by evidence, readiness earned in order); a page per project (how close, backlog, log, ideas); How we work from the canon; the observatory's family as its sub-views, ordered by the mark; ocoeco founded as the working system, its specification written, the mark, discovery and harvest moved into it - the engine is only the face; land waits for CI checks to appear; lab-agent guide teaches the living practices.
rejected: Readiness from any done milestone (a later one lifted it); unknown as failure; whole files copied from a stale copy; merging before checks appear.
title: Every project its own view; the observatory's family; ocoeco founded

considered: Filling every step with something.
done: Its workings: what delivers and proves each step of its path, and why we care. Steps that nothing serves yet are left empty, to be seen.
rejected: That: a step nothing serves is a wish, and should show.
title: It tells its essence

considered: Terse cards of concepts.
done: The idea of the observatory written as an ordered piece of writing in its own data - what it is, what it is for, a picture, its honest limit, where it stands - for a reader who knows nothing of it; shown by the observatory as an article.
rejected: Those as the idea: they name the parts for an insider.
title: Its idea, told for anyone

considered: A template repository for joining.
done: ocoeco init and check make joining one command (fifteen repositories had been joined by hand); Rhizoid joined with it, its path reading ocoeco's own backlog for its last stop. Criteria are read in their own project first, then anywhere; lenses found but not curated are shown as discovered. Sixteen projects, no problems.
rejected: That: a template drifts; a command writes what is current.
title: Joining in one command; Rhizoid joins

considered: Restructuring every formatting call for messages; translating the rendered HTML afterwards.
done: Languages specified (ocoeco SPEC section 9); the face renders once per language under /en/ and /ru/ with a thin switcher of languages in their own names, lang and hreflang, old addresses redirecting; Fluent catalogs with correct Russian plurals (103 коммита); sixty interface messages marked where written and resolved per page.
rejected: Translating rendered output (fragile, no grammar); plain string tables (wrong plurals); flags or codes in the switcher; switching by script.
title: The observatory in two languages

considered: Keeping grand views in the engine; reading raw files with a retry.
done: ocoeco gatherers (activity, releases, CI) in all eleven marked repositories through one reusable workflow, shown as each project's heartbeat; shared tables read through GitHub's API (current, authoritative); lenses specified (SPEC section 8), harvested from lens.toml, and drawn by the face - Linux Phones is now a lens in its family's organization, curated into the navigation.
rejected: Hard-coded views (a gatekeeper); the raw file server (cached for minutes, 501 to empty files on some runners); sending the API's headers to raw files.
title: Data made by work, and the first lens

considered: A single flat site; tad's own pages; one progress percentage.
done: The architecture written; the mark (schema 1) on seven projects; the engine in Rust (discover, harvest, site); a scheduled run that discovers, harvests, renders and publishes; the site restructured around grand projects with honest tables.
rejected: Unknown counted as failure; hand-ordered columns; prose-only design.
title: The observatory founded, discovering and publishing itself

considered: Transferring Rhizoid's repositories at once.
done: Rhizome's home (the author's manifesto, 26 concepts, 14 decisions, the Hypha roadmap, its path) and its lens, curated second; the lens gathers Rhizoid where it lives.
rejected: That, for now: it changes their addresses.
title: Rhizome in the picture

considered: An exception for protected repositories.
done: argenv marked, with its own path from its real state; Mnemonic Vocabulary recorded as a grand project at the idea stage, with its own lens curated second. Gathered data moved to an oco-data branch everywhere, and automation's commits left out of activity - found through argenv's protected branch.
rejected: That: one rule for every repository.
title: argenv joins; Mnemonic Vocabulary gets its place

considered: Turning marks green by filling steps.
done: ocoeco check now tells a project at home what its essence lacks; the front page shows every project's four marks and one number - 0 of 19 tell their whole essence. Eleven ideas read in Russian. In the phone's lab a listening test needs the word that the microphone is placed. Found by looking: the cards spoke English on the Russian side and counted twice - fixed.
rejected: That: zero of nineteen is the truth, and the list of what to build.
title: Essence measured where the work is done and where it is shown

done: Practice 19 written where agents read their instructions; this morning's findings recorded in the phone's lab, the lab tools and the phone project, concepts and decisions included.
title: A practice for concepts and decisions

considered: Inventing paths for the canon and the playbook so they would have Essence pages.
done: Five ideas read in Russian, each translated in its own project's data and marked as machine-made. Rhizome and tad wrote their workings; tad its idea. In the phone's lab the listening test was first withdrawn (the microphone was being worn), then put right by the author: it is reliable when placed, so it runs only on notice - and a proper rig is on the lab tools' backlog.
rejected: That: what they must reach is theirs to say.
title: Ideas in Russian; the ear, on notice

considered: Guessing the sensor models.
done: The Russian side lost its last English: counted words take the form their number asks for, the kinds of workings are words, and the workings of four projects are translated. On the phone, the cameras' darkness got a cause - no sensor is described - and a way in, from the vendor's own wiring of seven slots.
rejected: That.
title: A Russian page that is Russian; the cameras understood

considered: Staying with the describing.
done: After the ways of describing work, the work itself: the phone's own checks were widened (27 in the baseline) and four of its eight unknown parts now follow evidence - Wi-Fi works, Bluetooth partly, sensors and the fingerprint reader broken. What stays unknown says why: no SIM card in the phone; a jack and an NFC controller nobody has tried. The cameras' fault is narrowed to image sensors not bound.
rejected: That: the picture exists for the phones.
title: Back to the purpose: more of the phone, measured

considered: Treating the full picture as frequent switching.
done: From the author: do not bury yourself in one thing; perfect connected processes; perfect OCO itself. Answered with practice 20, a decision that the observatory stays a mirror, and two steps that turn it into mechanisms: the attention view and recording as a tool. The package conveyor delivered lab-agent v0.1.47 and v0.1.48; the lab machine now updates itself daily.
rejected: That: half-built things everywhere is its own failure; finish a connected piece, then choose by the weakest link.
title: The whole first

done: The first view is now Rhizome's own idea, as Rhizome wrote it; how close it is comes second. The lens writes nothing about the project - it gathers and shows.
rejected: Opening with a path a newcomer cannot yet read.

title: The idea, its name, and Hypha's roadmap

considered: Moving Rhizoid's repositories here at once.

On the periphery by the author's choice: recorded whole, not being built yet. Read from the gist in full and from one conversation; later conversations inside a project could not be read from here.
